data.claim:
A company AI talk (33 slides) vs ddflow. Verdict per slide group (P=PRESENT, PA=PARTIAL, A=ABSENT), evidence, covering ids.
1-5 charter/agenda: A (org practice, not tooling). Radar/adoption success measure: A (no adoption telemetry; P-observe.telemetry, UX-local-telemetry open).
6-7 precise prompt/toolkit overlap: PA. Rules+charter carry standing part (ddflow rule add --scope/--globs/--pin, mcp_instructions.md, rules charter); task body is free text, no readiness lint (no id).
8-10 vocabulary, lap, context layers, cache order: PA. Research docs context-compaction-cache.md/token-spend.md hold the facts (VERIFIED 2026-10-23); no enforced L0-L3 contract. FINDING: mcp_instructions.md lines 58-74 inject volatile counts/drift/companions into the handshake (bug B-mcp-instructions-volatile-prefix); brief opens with RESUME/lost-events (volatile first). CC-cache-policy, TE-cache-hygiene open.
11 quadratic bill: PA. Token-spend decision D-TE-* (cache TTL 1h done TE-subagent-ttl, poll<=240s done TE-poll-cadence, context caps done TE-context-caps); no per-run lap/cost model or 17x view. GV-step-cost, CC-usage-metrics, P-perf-metrics (30/53) open.
12 compaction/drift: PA. P-context-compaction 2/17 (CC-advisor, CC-resume-pack, CC-store open), govern.context_mark_1..3 = 0.6/0.75/0.85 (config), P-drift 1/19.
13 subagents cost: PA. ORC-usage-semantics done; ORC-subagent-attribution open; no delegate-pays threshold advisor.
14 cache alive: PA. TE-subagent-ttl, TE-poll-cadence done; D-model-routing safe-point switching with switch cost (GV-switch-cost open); ORC-model-pinning open; doctor warns when TTL unset.
15 L0-L3 ordering, cache breakers: A as contract/lint (CC-cache-policy open, the nearest).
16 price table: PA. DRV-model-catalog done (windows, prices, cache, limits as data with provenance, models.toml); TE-limit-aware-routing done (layered price and limit table). Output/reasoning ratio and tokenizer +30% not modelled as such.
17 levers vs two meters: A as a report (GV-regret, GV-eval, PM-quality-signals open; SW-ledger done: first-pass gate rate per family/model/kind).
18 models think longer per upgrade: A (no re-measure on model upgrade hook; SW-ledger is the data source).
19 effort classes M/L/X/R: PA. GV-complexity-score, GV-preset, GV-escalate (escalate one tier on repeated gate failure), GV-roles open (P-governor 2/33); no task effort/model/turn-cap field (task add has none); review.max_rounds=6 is the only cap analogue; R/spike-first = kind research exists (task add --kind).
20 nine rules: PA. 2 write once P (rules/AGENTS.md); 3 PA (P-lean-start 11/20, P-tool-diet 9/18, TE-bounded outputs); 5 PA; 7 PA; 8 P (hooks, pre-commit, gates); 9 PA.
21-23 baseline vs local: PA. Layers default<company<project<local<user (D-config-layer-order, D-user-highest-precedence-2026-11-06); DRV-packs done (digest-pinned company packs); P-org-config 0/18, GP-org, LP-override-record, LP-e2e open.
24 seven parts: commitments/principles P (rules with enforcement strength, pinned rules, decisions, goals/principles kinds; LP-kinds-coverage open); stack guides PA (rule --globs scope; codeguide companion); skills PA (ddflow ships skills/commands; GC-agent-files, P-agent-lifecycle.manifest-adopt, OB-model open); templates PA (P-doc-templates); knowledge/governance P (research/lesson/decision/ADR records); model evaluation PA (GV-eval open; reviewer ledger); tooling P (adopt installer, doctor, validation).
25 developer flow: install P (ddflow adopt / onboard, commit generated files; B-onboard 13/13 done); task card A (GV-complexity-score, GV-roles); skill invoke PA; stack guidance auto-load PA (rule globs injected on claim); validate P (gates, live_test, ci).
26 ideal run, loops rare: PA. Gate pipeline is deterministic+model; ddflow metrics stages shows gate re-runs, rework rounds; no first-pass-per-item/runs-per-merge headline (PM-quality-signals, FOC-gate-budget open).
27 skills by lifecycle: PA. Skills shipped for implement; lifecycle skill catalogue (shape/design/verify/ship) not; SPEC-docs, GC-spec-stage, PO-*, TM-* packs open.
28 guidance vs checks, pairing rule: P (r-evidence-over-assertion, enforcement strength, hooks block, gates 'exit code IS the evidence'; ddflow is AHEAD). Pairing rule not stated: A. Ownership of commitments: A (no owner field on rules; LF-health 'decisions without owner' open).
29 governance, evidence, cadence, ADR, stable ids: P/PA. ADRs = decisions with status proposed/accepted/superseded; rules have stable ids; cadence mechanism exists (SJ-cadence-compat, CM-packs-watch open); deliberate exceptions: waivers A (GP-waiver, RQM-strength, SEC-policy, LP-override-record open).
30 gate-failure feeds toolkit, prose gate: PA. lesson add + ddflow lesson verify (pattern re-scan) manual; no auto gate-finding->rule/lesson proposal (SW-ledger/WP-gate-yield done are detectors only; LP-contribute open); prose lint (Vale) pluggable: tool-gate binding SC-gate-binding open, companions list has no prose linter; standards gate is an agent gate (model judgement) today.
31 visibility/ownership/stacks/gates: A. constellation MR-views, MR-policy-floor, CN-sync open; no installed-version/baseline report across projects.
32 contribute: PA. LP-contribute, SM-improve-report open.
33 eight lessons: 1 start from done: A (no acceptance-criteria field on task add; body free text; GC-spec-stage open). 2 stages P (gate pipeline). 3 one home per fact: PA (layers; rule add --check/--duplicate-of dedupe; no cross-kind dup check memory/rule/CLAUDE.md). 4 keep findings: P (research/lesson/memory, ddflow recall, dedupe on add); auto-promotion A (LP-contribute open). 5 gate where it costs: P (tiered pipelines, fix-Bbd88c54354 trivial tier, kind_pipelines, FOC-gate-budget open). 6 people are gates: P (approvals engine, person-only commands, chat channel rule r-approval-chat-channel). 7 watch runs to merge, stop after N: PA (review.max_rounds, r-bounded-everything, metrics stages; no runs-to-merge and N-failures-ask knob). 8 improve the system: PA (lessons, rules; no closed loop).
SLIDE WEAKNESSES: numbers (17x, 4x, 15x, 7x, 280x) are single illustrative or vendor figures; effort tiers/turn caps (4/8/12/6) are unsourced defaults; 'Gates = NOT A MODEL' ignores that most real review gates (critic, standards) are models: ddflow labels them agent gates and requires cross-family; Vale-only prose gate is narrow; success = adoption counts, not outcome/cost per merged change; 'distance from intent' has no measurement method. ddflow is ahead on: enforced (not requested) gate pipeline, unavailable-is-not-pass, event-log provenance, layered config with person-only override, cross-family reviewers, bug-needs-failing-test, per-model cache/price facts as data.
IDEAS RANKED (value/effort): 1 byte-stable handshake + cache lint in doctor (high/low; CC-cache-policy plus bug). 2 runs-per-merge and first-pass rate per item headline in ddflow metrics (high/low; data exists in gate records; PM-quality-signals, SW-ledger). 3 task card record: model, effort, caps, skill, acceptance criteria, derived from kind/complexity, layered table in config (high/med; GV-complexity-score, GV-preset). 4 acceptance-criteria field plus readiness lint on claim (high/low-med). 5 N-failed-runs stop-and-ask knob (high/low; extends review.max_rounds, r-bounded-everything). 6 gate-finding to rule/lesson proposal (repeat finding threshold) and pre-flight of standards in agent loop (med/med; LP-contribute). 7 installed-baseline version/adoption report across projects (med-high/med; constellation MR-views, P-org-config). 8 rule owner/review-cadence/waiver with expiry (med/med; GP-waiver, LP-override-record). 9 cost/lap dashboard with quadratic effect, cached/fresh/output split and price table (med/high; GV-step-cost, CC-usage-metrics, P-perf-metrics). 10 pluggable prose-lint gate as companion (low-med/low; SC-gate-binding). 11 skills eval on realistic prompts across providers (med/high; tests/eval has only tool_diet).
BEST PRACTICE SOURCES (not re-fetched this run; verified earlier in docs/ddflow/research/context-compaction-cache.md, 2026-10-23): Anthropic prompt caching docs (docs.claude.com prompt-caching: prefix order tools>system>messages, up to 4 breakpoints, 5m/1h TTL, read 0.1x write 1.25x/2x); OpenAI prompt caching guide (automatic prefix, >=1024 tokens); Google Gemini context caching; Anthropic 'Effective context engineering for AI agents' and multi-agent research post (~15x tokens); Claude Code docs on subagents/agent teams and memory (CLAUDE.md hierarchy, path-scoped rules, skills progressive disclosure); Chroma 'context rot' study.

data.title: Always-on text is ordered by change frequency and the handshake stays byte-stable

data.body:
Fixes bug B-mcp-instructions-volatile-prefix: MCP initialize instructions (templates/prompts/mcp_instructions.md lines 58-74) embed volatile per-session text (crashed-worktree count, queue-loop count, rules drift, companion states, gate gaps, setup_todo, open choices) inside the system-prompt region: two lanes started minutes apart get different prefixes so cross-lane/subagent prefix cache sharing is lost and the instruction bytes are not ordered by change frequency. Fix: keep the handshake byte-stable (static contract only) and move the volatile lines to the first brief; covered in plan by CC-cache-policy (lint) but not by any task that moves them.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B-mcp-instructions-volatile-prefix --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B-mcp-instructions-volatile-prefix --regression-test <test>` first).

WHAT: make the MCP initialize instructions byte-stable (D-prompt-layers L0): keep only the static contract; move the per-session lines (crashed-worktree count, queue-loop count, rules drift, companion states, gate gaps, setup_todo) into the first brief or a tool result, ordered after the stable text. COORDINATE: in-flight B181 already moves undecided workflow choices from the handshake to the brief and holds a lease on mcp_instructions.md; claim this only after B181 merges (no needs edge on an in-flight item); this task covers every OTHER volatile line. ACCEPTANCE: a test renders the handshake twice with different crashed, loop, drift, companion and gate-gap state and asserts byte-identical output (fails before: the counts differ); the moved lines appear in the brief with the same remedy calls; the handshake never contains a digit-counted state line. Estimated size: S (about 120 lines). CONFIGURABILITY (r-everything-configurable, D-config-layer-order, D-user-highest-precedence-2026-11-06): every number, list and mode is a knob in the named [section] declared in ddflow/config_sections/, settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt, layered shipped < company < project < local < user, defaults shipped as overridable data, no hard-coded constants (r-everything-configurable); a README knob-table row (regenerated from the declared metadata, never hand-edited) and an upgrade fragment under ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/.

WHAT: encode D-prompt-layers as data and a contract test: L0 static (charter, MCP contract, tool list), L1 slow (rules, decisions, project facts), L2 per task (body, acceptance criteria), L3 per turn (brief, resume, last gate). Every generated always-on text (handshake, charter, driver, agent files) declares its layer; the test fails when a faster-changing text precedes a slower one, or when an L0/L1 text carries a count, timestamp, path or per-session value. Layer assignments are the data table [prompt_layers] (overridable per layer of config). ACCEPTANCE: the test fails against a fixture that puts a loop count before the charter and passes after; extends CC-cache-policy (the doctor lint reads the same table). Estimated size: M (about 220 lines). data.title: Prompt layer contract: L0-L3 ordering by change frequency, enforced by a contract test

data.body:
WHAT: lint over the interface ddflow serves per (version, profile, config): tools/list order sorted and byte-identical across two builds, no timestamps/ids/counters/paths in tool descriptions or MCP instructions, digest (SU-digest) stable under a no-op config reload; volatile text only in the conversation layer (SessionStart, footers). A doctor line (added after TE-subagent-ttl lands: both touch api/reporting/health.py) reports lint result and the effective TTL. RULE with SU-announce/SU-restart-notice: for a client the table says does NOT defer MCP tools, a non-urgent tool-list change waits for a cache-cold moment (idle > ttl, compaction, restart); hard upgrades unaffected; Claude Code defers by default (VERIFIED) so no wait. Also the standard brief: shared fixed prefix, per-item part last (LS-launch-brief-budget owns size). TEST: lint fails on an injected timestamp in a description; sorted-order test; digest stable; swap deferred for a non-deferring fixture client and immediate for a deferring one. FALSIFIER: unexplained cache-creation spikes in CC-usage-metrics do not fall.

EXTENDED 2026-11-11 (D-prompt-layers, R-ai-talk-2026-11-11, talk slides 10, 14, 15): add the doctor cache-breaker lint as named checks: a timestamp or counter in the byte-stable prefix, an unsorted generated list (tools, rules, companions, gates) in always-on text, and a tool-set, effort or model change recorded mid-session. Reads the layer table of TE-prompt-layer-contract; the checks are a data list [cache_lint].checks with a mode off|warn|block per layer of config. Acceptance: one fixture per check fails before the check exists. Estimated added size: S (about 100 lines). The handshake fix itself is fix-B-mcp-instructions-volatile-prefix.

WHAT: a help topic and doctor notes: do not change model/effort/MCP set mid-session, keep MCP tools deferred (tool search), set idleCompaction, show the 'Prompt cache (main)' /usage line in the status line; note for P-soft-upgrade that list_changed with deferred tools does not bust the cache. WHY: research 3.2: the lead's only large cache writes were 6 idle expiries (13% of the lead, 0.9% of total); no tool-list change busted it. TEST: help topic exists, parity test passes.

EXTENDED 2026-11-11 (R-ai-talk-2026-11-11): the help topic and doctor note also say why handshake text must stay byte-stable and point at D-prompt-layers and the doctor cache-breaker lint in CC-cache-policy; the mid-session model, effort and tool-set change warning reuses the same lint, not a second one.

WHAT (D-runs-per-merge, talk slides 26, 33): a headline report from existing gate records, no new events: per merged item the number of runs (gate runs and review rounds, gate re-runs after a failure) and whether it passed first time; rolled up per phase, per model and per gate kind, deterministic gates labelled apart from model gates; configurable window ([metrics].runs_window_days, default 30) and outlier flag. Reuses SW-ledger (first-pass rate per family, model, kind) and FOC-gate-budget (minutes and runs per item); does not recompute them, it adds the per-item rollup and the headline line in ddflow metrics, MCP and brief. ACCEPTANCE: a fixture log with one item passing first time and one needing three runs reports 100% and 33% first-pass and 1 vs 3 runs (the test fails before the report exists); window and grouping knobs change the output. Estimated size: M (about 250 lines).
data.title: ddflow metrics runs: runs to merge and first-pass rate per item, phase and model

data.body:
Extends B-sub-metrics (same agent and definition-digest key, one agent stats surface). Credible metrics only: first-pass rate per gate by author agent and model; rework rounds per item; bugs filed against an item commits within N days (maps to DORA change fail rate and rework rate; needs the bug to item to author link, build it from the existing bug records); reviewer yield (findings confirmed or fixed versus refuted per review, per KLOC changed) and its latency and cost; cost per merged item from the ledger. Vanity measures are not shown as quality: raw tokens, lines written, approval rate. Every figure shows its sample size and a not enough data state under the knob minimum. Reviewer independence stays untouched (this reports, it never routes). Tests with a seeded log including an agent that introduces bugs. CONFORMANCE (r-reuse-core, r-small-files, r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-no-shell, r-tell-dont-discover, D-no-duckdb, D-sched-no-daemon): extend the existing metrics code, never a second store or scheduler; stdlib first, optional third-party only behind a port with a fake; one declaration gives CLI, MCP action and prompt; every threshold and interval is a knob in [perf_metrics] with org lock; every answer names the exact next call in CLI and MCP form; a probe that could not run is recorded unavailable, never zero or passed; raw samples stay in .ddflow/local, only small per-run rollups reach the committed log; no prompt text, command arguments, paths of the user, or secrets in any metric; files stay under [quality].max_file_bytes (package, thin facade). Research: R-perf-landscape, R-perf-inventory.

EXTENDED 2026-11-11 (D-runs-per-merge): first-pass rate and rework per item are delivered by PM-runs-to-merge; this task keeps bug-after-merge, reviewer yield and cost per merged item and reads the same per-item rollup instead of recomputing it.

Mean 62 gate-minutes, p50 6 and p90 13 gate runs per merged item, 15% forced completions (261 of 1720). Report them, flag outliers, propose a risk-tiered pipeline (the light profile, UX-light-profile). A forced completion records a reason class. SIZE M, RISK medium. FALSIFIER: median gate minutes per item does not drop below 30. CONFORMANCE (r-derive-dont-store, r-bounded-everything, r-operator-attention, r-evidence-over-assertion, D-scope-focus-2026-11, R-audit-scope): each task states its falsifier; nothing is abandoned or merged without the operator; no GUI or board is built.

EXTENDED 2026-11-11 (D-runs-per-merge): the per-item run count it reports is the same value as PM-runs-to-merge; share one function, report minutes here and runs-to-merge and first-pass rate there.

WHAT (D-task-card-fields, talk slide 25): optional fields on the task record, NOT a new record kind: model, effort, turn_cap, spike_cap, skill, acceptance_criteria (list of checkable statements). Set by ddflow task add and ddflow update (the universal update path, DX-update-universal merged: --set/--append-body style ops), shown by ddflow show and the brief at claim; on MCP through the existing ddflow_task family tool and ddflow_update (NO new top-level tool). Fields are optional and default to the class table (TC-class-table); an explicit field wins over a class default. ddflow does not enforce the model or effort itself; it reports them in the claim and brief for the harness/driver to apply. ACCEPTANCE: a test adds a task with acceptance_criteria and a turn_cap, updates one, shows both, round-trips through the event log and replay (fails before the fields exist); the MCP family tool accepts the same fields; an unknown effort value is refused. Estimated size: M (about 300 lines).
data.title: Task card fields on tasks: model, effort, turn cap, spike cap, skill, acceptance criteria

data.body: WHAT (D-task-card-fields, talk slides 19, 25): a layered [task_classes] table, shipped as overridable data, classes M (mechanical), L (local), X (cross-cutting), R (research): effort low / low-medium / medium-high / high; turn caps 4/8/12; spike cap 6; R output is a spec, not code (R maps to kind research); escalation M->L on gate failure, L->X after 2 failures, X->human after 2 failures. Adjust rules as data: raise one level when the change touches security, concurrency, money, migrations or a commitment (matched by globs/tags/words, lists are knobs); lower one when a spec and a runnable check exist; retry one level up after a failed check. The class is chosen from kind plus GV-complexity-score when that lands (extend, do not duplicate: GV-complexity-score owns the score, GV-preset the optimize_for offset, GV-roles the role table); until then from kind and an explicit task class field. PROVENANCE: the table carries a field source = 'unsourced starting points from a company talk, uncalibrated', shown by ddflow config --explain beside every value; overridable in every layer (default < company < project < local < user, D-config-layer-order, D-user-highest-precedence-2026-11-06). ACCEPTANCE: config --explain prints the provenance string and winning layer per class value; a user-layer override beats a project value; adjust rule 'touches security' raises M to L in a test that fails before the table exists; removing the table leaves task add working with no card defaults. Estimated size: M (about 280 lines).
data.title: [task_classes] table: M/L/X/R class defaults for effort, caps and escalation, with effort-adjust rules as data

data.body: WHAT (D-task-card-fields, talk slide 19): apply the [task_classes] escalation rules: when an item's failed runs reach the class threshold, raise its class one level (effort and caps follow the table) and record why; past the top class, stop and ask the operator (reuses the stop-and-ask of BND-failed-run-cap). Consumes GV-escalate's signals (repeated gate failures, loops) when it lands instead of re-deriving them; emits the same escalate_request, adds no second mechanism. Per-class thresholds are knobs in [task_classes]; every change shows the cache-cost note of GV-preset. ACCEPTANCE: a fixture item in class M with one failed gate run moves to L, then X after two more, then asks (tests fail before); a user-layer threshold override changes the outcome. Estimated size: M (about 220 lines).
data.title: Class escalation on failed runs: M->L->X->human, a visible reason and the next call

data.body: WHAT (D-runs-per-merge, talk slide 33 lesson 7; r-bounded-everything, r-alert-owner-next-call): per-item cap on failed runs (a run is a gate run or agent attempt that ends failed); at the cap the item is held with a visible reason (which runs failed, which gate) and the exact next call for the operator (raise the cap, reroute, split, abandon), through the existing approvals/inbox path, never a silent retry. Knobs under [bounded]: failed_run_cap (default set in shipped data), failed_run_cap_by_kind, and a per-task-class override in [task_classes] (TC-escalation raises class before this stops). EXISTING, not duplicated: implement-loop four stop cases, review.max_rounds (review rounds only), approvals.auto_approve_after_retries (different: approval retries), DX-no-hold-and-wait (the ask must be a recorded question, not a wait). ACCEPTANCE: a fixture item with N+1 failed gate runs is held with reason and next call, N does not trigger (test fails before); cap 0 disables; a class override wins. Estimated size: M (about 240 lines).
